tagline: See what you're not seeing — on one page.
lore: The Sphinx guarded Thebes with riddles — here she poses the gaps in your coverage back to you: the exposure you didn't know you had.
problem: Each hound answers its own question well, but a CISO doesn't want twenty answers — they want one picture and one next move. Without a view that brings them together, the most dangerous risk survives: the unknown unknowns nobody thought to ask a single tool about.
does: Sphinx reads what the whole pack found on its last release and puts it on one page, On the Scent: how exposed the estate is, where risk concentrates, what is converging, what is on the clock, the blind spots, and the next moves — including a recommended play and how much exposure it would remove. Every number opens the exact assets behind it.

glance.caption: On the Scent's At a glance after a release: how exposed (estate score, KEV, crown jewels, blind), where it concentrates, converging signals, on the clock, blind spots, pack coverage and next moves — each card opens its evidence in Bloodhound or the owning hound, already filtered.

capabilities: every card opens its evidence: the exact assets (KEV, score ≥ 60, crown jewels, with KEV or blind, EOL, quantum-vulnerable …) or the owning hound, already filtered.
all assets → seen by a hound → credentialed → classified → owned → business-tiered, each step linked to the hound that owns the gap.
assets no hound saw, blind hosts, unclassified, unowned, no business tier, shadow AI.
the worst assets by fused score, with each hound's points on each host; the estate as one square per asset.
signal stacks, the overlap map and cross-hound surprises — where several hounds fire on the same assets.
patch KEV / critical, replace EOL, renew certificates, segment exposure or assign owners — with the exposure it would remove and the signals it neutralizes.
the digest of what moved since the last release.
how: On the Scent reads the cached results of the last Release the Hounds plus Nemesis's fused scores; it writes nothing. Evidence lists are computed on demand by the hound that owns each number, so they match the card.
who: CISOs who want the estate on one page, VM leads running the morning stand-up, and anyone building executive reporting that survives questions.
better: On the Scent is where the pack converges — Nemesis's scores, Laelaps, Chronos, Linnaeus, Terminus, Anubis, Pythia, Charon, Heimdall and the rest. Bloodhound shows the evidence behind each card, and Gabriel can send the briefing.
cta: Open On the Scent tomorrow morning — and see what you weren't seeing.
